goal.statement: Activate premium support from what the customer already bought, enforce response targets, and manage a support case from first report to close.
goal.outcome: A support team that can see exactly what each customer is covered for, refuse work nobody bought, and hold defensible evidence of when it responded — without anyone claiming a signature, a bill or a customer login that does not exist.

metric.name: share_of_cases_with_a_recorded_first_response_inside_target
metric.definition: Proportion of support cases whose recorded first response is at or before the elapsed-time target on their entitlement, over cases opened in the period.
metric.target: stated by the support organization; this plan does not invent one

decisions.rationale: The service package already owns coverage, entitlements and cases, and reaches the commercial source only through contracts/service-obligations@1. Using it is configuration of what exists, not new modelling.

What an obligation entitles a customer to is a business decision, so it belongs in a versioned, fingerprinted policy rather than in code that reads a label. The package supplies the contract; the organization supplies the rules.

steps.description: Read what the contract's pending service obligations would become, before writing anything. Planning records nothing, so it is safe to run as often as it takes to agree.

A human activates the coverage. An obligation the policy cannot decide is refused rather than guessed, and a human override carries a stated reason. What is produced is operational and is not a signed agreement: the commercial record is not touched by any of it.

Record cases against an entitlement, answer them, move them over the declared transition table, and append every note as evidence. The entitlement is enforced server-side: an uncovered category, an uncovered priority or a full open-case limit is refused.
Record what the elapsed-time targets said at a stated instant, and record an escalation when a human decides to escalate. Nothing evaluates or escalates on a clock, because no scheduler exists.

observedFacts.statement: Activating a contract already raises pending service obligations, which sit unconsumed until something activates them.
The service package owns coverage, entitlements, cases, case activity, SLA evaluations and escalations, and offers three read-only capabilities.
observedFacts.source: app inspect: packages[] service@1, capabilities[], resources[]

observedFacts.statement: Service reaches the commercial source only through contracts/service-obligations@1; contracts does not know Service exists.
SLA targets are elapsed wall-clock minutes from the injected UTC clock, with no calendar, no holidays and no paused clock.

A service coverage is an operational record: it is not a signed agreement, nobody signed it, it has no envelope, signer or artifact, and it neither amends nor replaces the Commercial Contract it was activated from.

assumptions.statement: The organization sells ongoing support as a recurring component, so a recurring obligation is what establishes coverage.
One coverage per contract is sufficient for this organization; multiple concurrent coverages per contract are not planned here.

derivedMetrics.statement: The share of cases answered inside their first-response target is computable from a recorded SLA evaluation per case, because the evaluation stores the exact inputs it used.

inferences.statement: An obligation the policy cannot classify should refuse rather than default, because a defaulted support tier is a promise nobody in the business made.

recommendations.statement: Configure and extend the service package rather than modelling support anywhere else: the domain already has an owner, and a second model would split the evidence.
Put the entitlement rules in a versioned activation policy so a stored coverage always names the exact rules that produced it, and changing the rules later cannot rewrite what an old coverage meant.
State the elapsed-time basis wherever an SLA figure is shown. A target presented without it will be read as a business-hours commitment, which this application cannot honour.

unavailableEvidence.statement: No baseline for first-response performance exists, because no case history has been recorded in this application yet.
unavailableEvidence.reason: Support cases begin at M15; nothing recorded a case before it, and reconstructing a first-response history would be an invention rather than evidence.

unavailableEvidence.statement: Whether the organization's targets are meant as business hours cannot be known here, and no calendar exists to express one.
unavailableEvidence.reason: No calendar exists in this framework, so an intended business-hours reading cannot be represented, let alone verified against what the organization meant.

unavailableEvidence.statement: Whether a case was genuinely reported by the customer cannot be established: no customer is authenticated and no channel is integrated.
unavailableEvidence.reason: No customer is authenticated and no channel is integrated, so who actually reported a case is an assertion by the recorder and nothing here can check it.

checks: planning writes no record, no audit row and no event
an obligation the policy cannot decide refuses activation until a human overrides it with a reason
no commercial row differs before and after an activation
a case against an uncovered category, an uncovered priority or a full entitlement is refused server-side
a recorded SLA evaluation names the instant and the inputs it used, and never claims to be current
an escalation records that a human escalated, and routes and notifies nothing

artifacts.description: The Service package definition, its capabilities and its declared dependency.
Two worked activation policies, one of which deliberately cannot decide an ordinary support obligation.
The package-scoped service section: coverage, entitlements, cases, SLA evidence and escalation.
Fault injection, two-connection races, exact reads past 500 rows, SLA boundaries and hostile input.
